MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 28, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR MITCHELL at 6:30 p.m. and the City Council convened into closed session in the City
Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer

CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR
  Government Code Section 54957.6
  Agency Designated Representative: City Manager
  Employee Organization: City of Rolling Hills Estates Employees’ Association
  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

  ***
MAYOR MITCHELL adjourned the Closed Session portion of the meeting at 7:00 p.m.

At 7:07 p.m., MAYOR MITCHELL called the meeting back to order in open session in the City
Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Members of Palos Verdes Peninsula High School Team CyberPanther #1, winners of the California
Mayors Cyber Cup, led the pledge of allegiance.

Kimberly Pease and Donna Woods of California Cyber Hub provided a presentation explaining the
Mayors Cyber Cup competition and highlighting the Team’s accomplishments. Members of the
Team presented the City with the Mayors Cyber Cup Trophy for display at City Hall for the next
year.

MAYOR MITCHELL provided Certificates of Recognition to the team members and their coach.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
City Council Members Absent:  None.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MAY 28, 2019
 City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Andy Clark, Community Services Director

  Jeannie Naughton, Senior Planner
  Mike Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING  MAY  2019  “MATERNAL  MENTAL  HEALTH
  AWARENESS MONTH”

MAYOR MITCHELL presented a proclamation in support of Maternal Mental Health Awareness
and declaring May as Maternal Mental Health Awareness Month.

COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ shared her experience with a maternal mental health disorder
and stressed the importance of mental health resources and a strong support team. Dr. Carol
Berkowitz, a Harbor-UCLA pediatrician, was present to accept the Proclamation.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council.
  There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote.
  (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  61522 (VOID – PRINTER TESTING) IN THE AMOUNT OF $81,180.65 FOR A
  GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $408,184.60 WITH PROPER AUDIT

MAY 28, 2019

A.  MC GOWAN CONSULTING LLC PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR MS4

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO THE
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH MC GOWAN CONSULTING
  LLC FOR MS4 PERMIT COMPLIANCE ASSISTANCE FOR FY 2019-20 IN AN
  AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $90,500.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 28, 2019
 B.  SECOND AMENDMENT TO LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Second Amendment to the
  Agreement for Landscape Maintenance Services with Bennett Landscape for an
  additional five years at the level of service desired by the City Council.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material). He
  stated that upon further review by the City Attorney, it is recommended that the City
  Council review and discuss the options surrounding herbicide use, provide direction to
  staff on that issue; and staff will return with a new agreement for consideration rather than
  an amendment to the existing agreement.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ regarding the maintenance of the area off
  Shady Vista, Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith clarified that the area is currently
  maintained by the contractor and that will remain the same.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the option to mulch
  Community Services Director Clark stated that the contractor generates its own mulch so
  there would be no additional cost to the City for the mulch.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN also inquired as to the possibility of using mulch
  combined with a pre-emergent herbicide.

  In response to MAYOR MITCHELL’S request, Sean Bennett, Bennett Landscape
  explained the three options and the pros and cons of each option. He stated that it would
  be possible to combine mulch with a pre-emergent herbicide. He recommended Option
  2, using mulch and limited use of chemical weed spays, for the best long-term benefits to
  the City with a 90% reduction of the use of chemical weed sprays.

  MAYOR MITCHELL noted that the main concern raised by residents has been over the
  use of Roudup specifically; and asked Mr. Bennet if there are other herbicide options
  available. Mr. Bennet responded that there are other organic herbicides available but they
  are typically less effective and more costly.

  Recognizing that there are members of the public present to address the City Council on
  this matter,

  Debby Stegura, 4706 Sugar Hill Drive, addressed the City Council to urge the City to be
  an environmental leader and discontinue the use of herbicides completely.

  Allen Sussman, resident, addressed the City Council to urge the City to discontinue the
  use of Roundup completely as many other cities have.

  MAYOR MITCHELL suggested that the City consider mulching and discontinuing the use
  of herbicides.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 28, 2019
   Discussion ensued concerning the cost and timing of the mulch option compared to the
  mechanical weed control option.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that it may be best from an environmental
  perspective to move away from herbicides completely and manage the weeds with mulch
  and mechanical control. He commented that there is likely to be some level of tolerance
  for weeds.

  Further discussion ensued concerning the option of using mulch with a pre-emergent
  herbicide.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that it would be fiscally and
  environmentally responsible to go with the mulching option and reducing herbicide use
  over the coming years.

  In response to City Manager Prichard’s request for clarification, Mr. Bennett stated that
  the 90% reduction in herbicide use would be over the course of the five year agreement,
  not in the first year. Discussion ensued concerning the options presented as well as an
  additional option to use a combination of mulch and mechanical control.

  Discussion ensued concerning eliminating the use of herbicides immediately and the
  options to get to that objective from a timing and cost perspective.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THE COUNCIL DIRECTED STAFF TO WORK WITH THE CONTRACTOR TO
  FURTHER RESEARCH WEED CONTROL OPTIONS TO ELIMINATE THE USE
  OF HERBICIDES AND BRING A REVISED CONTRACT BACK FOR APPROVAL.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None.

C.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING TO PROVIDE SUMMER SWIM PROGRAM
  SERVICES AT PALOS VERDES PENINSULA HIGH SCHOOL POOL

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the City Manager and City Attorney to
  enter into and execute the following contractual documents consistent with prior practice:
  1) Memorandum of Understanding between the Cities of Rancho Palos Verdes and
  Rolling Hills Estates and the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District for use of the
  Palos Verdes Peninsula High School Pool; and 2) Amendment to the Agreement between
  the Cities of Rancho Palos Verdes and Rolling Hills Estates and the San Pedro &
  Peninsula YMCA for the coordination of the Summer Swim Program.

  MAYOR MITCHELL stated that she and COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN recently met
  with representatives from the School District and Rancho Palos Verdes to come to an
  agreement but there are still some details being worked out. She further commented that
  there have been some recent developments and asked City manager Prichard to report
  on the status.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 28, 2019
   City Manager Prichard requested that the City Council provide the City Manager the
  authority to approve a bridge agreement, under the same terms as the current agreement
  with the School District and a services agreement with the YMCA so that the swim
  program can proceed as scheduled this summer.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stat that the City’s intent with the new agreement is to
  be consistent with the prior agreement.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, second by MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZED THE CITY MANAGER TO SIGN A
  BRIDGE AGREEMENT FOR THE CONTINUATION OF EXISTING SERVICES
  UNTIL A NEW AGREEMENT IS APPROVED BY THE PARTIES.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None.

D.  RESIDENCES AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB RESIDENTIAL DESIGN
  GUIDELINES

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the Residences at Rolling Hills
  Country Club Design Guidelines.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the fencing between the
  properties and the architectural style varieties, Senior Planner Naughton stated that staff
  is comfortable that the developer has incorporated enough variety but kept enough
  consistency to ensure a cohesive development so there is not a town home type look.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ commented that it will be confusing to property owners that
  the guidelines refer to design review body as “Rolling Hills.”

  COUNCIL MEMBER  ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by,  COUNCILMEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE ROLLING HILLS
  COUNTRY CLUB DESIGN GUIDELINES.

  There being no objection, MAYOR MITCHELL so ordered.

OLD BUSINESS

NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MAY 28, 2019
 CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

A.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: SILVER SPUR ROAD AND RANGE

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Traffic and Safety Committee's

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
MAY 28, 2019
 B.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: 777 SILVER SPUR ROAD AT
